clue.text: Part of final leg rowed briskly

indicators.note: only a portion of the following run of words is wanted, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A rower takes the closing stretch of a race at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical tempo marking meaning to be played quickly and lively.

clue.text: Article poet put together quite slowly

explanation.surface: Assembling an essay about a poet at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Moving sideways behind really odd characters

indicators.note: odd characters are those in the first, third and fifth positions of the word

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Strange people shuffling crabwise at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to the side, as in a lateral pass or lateral movement.

clue.text: Grind magnet smashed in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle asks for the central letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A broken magnet is ground down at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash is to grind the teeth together, especially in anger.

clue.text: Hire third party to expose informer

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them
a journalist's source is an informant

explanation.surface: Bringing in a private investigator to unmask a mole.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsource is to contract work out to an external company rather than doing it in-house.

clue.text: Caver is disturbed at what's inside

indicators.note: something disturbed is knocked out of its proper order, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A potholer is unsettled by what lies within a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscera are the internal organs of the body, its contents in the most literal sense.

clue.text: Tenor starts to vary oratorio in choral event

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A tenor begins to improvise in an oratorio performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenor is one particular singing part, an example of a type of singer's register.

clue.text: Coffee chain is unfair when ejecting brat doing headstand

indicators.note: the outer word is pictured spitting out the other from its middle, so one sits inside the other
in a down clue, standing on one's head turns the word upside down, reading from the bottom

explanation.surface: A child doing a handstand gets thrown out of a café.
explanation.definitionFit: Starbucks is the American multinational chain of coffee shops.

clue.text: Structure provided in English game …

indicators.note: in places the condition word inside the game

explanation.surface: A building supplied for an English sport, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing building or any elaborate structure.

clue.text: … explains all you need to complete what you're doing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: responds to or accounts for, verb

definitions.text: all you need to complete what you're doing
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the solutions that fill a crossword grid

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue for surface; 'what you're doing' is the crossword itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer is to reply or account for, and the answers are what fill every light in the puzzle.

clue.text: Take away section after database is depleted

indicators.note: the section is placed following the reduced word rather than before it
a depleted word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters behind

parts.note: a tract is a section or stretch of land

explanation.surface: Part of a records system is removed once the data store has run low.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to diminish or subtract from something, as in detracting from its worth.

clue.text: Type that leans forward for emphasis, perhaps

definitions.text: Type that leans forward for emphasis, perhaps

parts.note: surface reading: a person of a type who leans in to stress a point
setter's reading: printing type that slopes to the right, used to stress words

explanation.surface: An eager kind of speaker leans in to drive home a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' reads as a kind of person; it is printing type, the sloping letters used for stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic letters slant rightwards and are the standard printed way to stress a word.

clue.text: The high point of kinky hotel porn

indicators.note: kinky means twisted or bent out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: The highlight of a seedy hotel's adult film channel.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole sits at the very top of the globe on a conventional map, its highest point.

clue.text: Live in green environment, initially — a bit bland, perhaps

definitions.note: a colour adjective, offered as an example of blandness

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Eco-friendly living can be a touch dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is just one of the words supplying a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beige is a pale fawn colour, so often used to describe anything dull or unexciting.

clue.text: She sounds out large number

indicators.note: sounding out means saying the letters as spoken, so their spoken names count

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large and N for number; spoken, the two letter names run together

explanation.surface: A woman calls out a big figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's first name, and crosswords use 'she' to stand for any female name.

clue.text: Ring into broken landline that isn't connected

indicators.note: into puts the ring shape inside the phone word
a broken item is in pieces, so the letters are put back in a new order

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Calling a faulty home phone that has no connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' and 'landline' build a phone scene, but Ring is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-allied nation has no alliance with others, so it is not connected to them.

clue.text: Soccer, hit with violation, bounces back

indicators.note: a violation breaks something, so these words are broken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Football, hit by a foul, recovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounces back' sounds like a team's revival but is the literal rebound of a missile.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectile that ricochets glances off a surface and rebounds in another direction.

clue.text: Maybe doctor takes in personal debts for stranger

indicators.note: takes in means one item swallows the other within it

parts.note: a doctor is one who cures, an example
IOUs are written promises to repay

explanation.surface: A physician lends to an unfamiliar person on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curiouser' is Alice's famous ungrammatical comparative in Lewis Carroll's Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious means odd, and its playful comparative means odder, as Alice exclaims in Carroll's tale.

clue.text: Storyteller talked of torture while travelling

indicators.note: talked signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: rack is torture, on tour means travelling

explanation.surface: A narrator recounts torments suffered on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone who tells anecdotes skilfully and entertainingly.

clue.text: Socialist currency has little value

definitions.note: a phrase naming a thing worth almost nothing

parts.note: a coin, a unit of currency

explanation.surface: A left-wing country's money is nearly worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A red cent, a copper coin, is the idiom for the smallest possible amount of money.

clue.text: Food sign contains one error

indicators.note: contains places the following pair within the sign word

parts.note: a sin is a moral error

explanation.surface: A restaurant's notice has a single mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a style of cooking, and so the food produced in it.

clue.text: Exclusive: 'Waste gas coming back'

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: CS gas is a tear gas

explanation.surface: A news headline about returning sewage gas.
explanation.walkthrough: CS is the riot-control tear gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is an exclusive story that one newspaper publishes ahead of its rivals.

clue.text: Booming round and round

parts.note: a round shape, the letter O

explanation.surface: Something loud goes round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round and round' reads as one idiom; each round is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An orotund voice is full, resonant and imposing, so it sounds deep and loud.

clue.text: Gift that is found under cupboard

indicators.note: in a down clue, found under means the abbreviation comes after the furniture word

parts.note: a press is a large cupboard, especially in Ireland and Scotland

explanation.surface: A present hidden beneath a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressie' is informal British for a present; a press is an old word for a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressie is a colloquial British diminutive for a present or gift.

clue.text: Practise boring routine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to train by repetition, verb
second meaning: a tedious repeated exercise, or the tool that bores holes

explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' plays on both dullness and making holes, and the second meaning works either way.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill is to train by repetition, and a drill is also a set exercise or a tool for making holes.

clue.text: Offend me and it sets a bad tone

parts.note: to wrong someone is to offend against them
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Insulting the speaker lowers the tone of the conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the sol-fa syllable, also spelt mi, and stands for any note.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who hits a false pitch produces an off-key sound, a literally bad tone.

clue.text: Cringe as Church goes after land

indicators.note: goes after places the church abbreviation following the other piece

parts.note: to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: Embarrassment as the church pursues a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun for property; it is the verb meaning to secure.
explanation.definitionFit: To wince is to grimace or flinch in pain or embarrassment, much as one cringes.

clue.text: Spies without a place to go

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Secret agents with no safe house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a place to go' is the euphemism for a toilet; the Gents is a British men's lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gents is a men's public toilet, and 'go' is the euphemism for using one.

clue.text: Joining together of Jewish boy and Welsh girl

parts.note: the boy priest Eli of the Old Testament, and a Hebrew name

explanation.surface: A wedding of a Jewish man and a Welsh woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joining together' suggests a marriage, but in grammar it means running sounds together by dropping one.
explanation.definitionFit: Elision is the omission of a sound so that two words or syllables are run together, as in 'don't'.

clue.text: Dispatch courier to deliver caricatures

parts.note: United Parcel Service, a delivery company

explanation.surface: Arranging a parcel company to carry some cartoons.
explanation.definitionFit: Send-ups are parodies or mocking imitations, which is what caricatures are.

clue.text: Engineer altered pedal that makes wheel turn

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so these letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: An engineer modified the pedal driving a wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a person; it is a verb telling you to rebuild the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot lever that drives a machine such as a spinning wheel or old sewing machine.

clue.text: Save papers replacing copyright for what's left

indicators.note: replacing tells you one item is swapped out and another put in its place

parts.note: the copyright symbol is a C

explanation.surface: Keep the documents in place of the copyright notice to see what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is the remainder of something after the main part has been removed.
